From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: chao, Chao, chāo, cháo, chǎo, chào, and tchau

Old Galician-Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃã.u/
  • Rhymes: -ãu

Etymology 1

[edit]

    Inherited from Latin plānum (“level ground”, noun), from plānus (“flat”, adjective).

    Noun

    [edit]

    chão m (plural chãos)

    1. ground, floor
      • a. 1284, Alfonso X of Castile, Cantigas de Santa Maria, Códice de los músicos, cantiga 236 (facsimile):
        Como hũa moller que perigoóu no mar. ⁊ tragia un fillo pequeno nos braços. ⁊ fezea ſanta maria per címa das aguas andar de pé aſſi como ẏria per un muí bon chão.
        How a woman who sank in the sea. And had a small child in her arms. And Holy Mary brought her over the water to walk as she would in a good floor.
    2. flatland, plain
    Related terms
    [edit]
    • prão
    Descendants
    [edit]
    • Galician: chan, chá, chao, chao, chão (reintegrationist)
    • Portuguese: chão
      • Macanese: cham, (modern spelling) chám

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

      Inherited from Latin plānus (“flat”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Doublet of plano.

      Adjective

      [edit]

      chão m (plural chãos, feminine chãa, feminine plural chãas)

      1. flat, smooth
        • a. 1284, Alfonso X of Castile, Cantigas de Santa Maria, Códice de los músicos, 325 cantiga Cantiga 325 (facsimile):
          Pois a Catiua eſperta. / foi achouſſ en űu camỹo / ancho ⁊ chão ſen pedras / ⁊ andou o mui feſtỹno
          So the smart captive / went and found herself in a path, / ample and flat, without rocks, / and walked through it very quickly.
      Descendants
      [edit]
      • Galician: chan
      • Portuguese: chão

      Portuguese

      [edit]

      Alternative forms

      [edit]
      • tchão (eye dialect, Northern Portugal)
      • cham, chaõ (obsolete)

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʃɐ̃w̃/ [ˈʃɐ̃ʊ̯̃]
       
      • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʃɐ̃w̃/
      • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʃɐ̃w̃/
        • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃɐ̃w̃/

      • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
      • Rhymes: -ɐ̃w̃
      • Hyphenation: chão

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

        Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese chão (“ground”), from Latin plānum (“level ground”) < plānus, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Compare Galician chan and Spanish llano. Doublet of plano, porão, piano, and lhano.

        Noun

        [edit]

        chão m (plural chãos)

        1. ground, soil, earth
          Synonyms: solo, terra
        2. floor
          Synonyms: assoalho, piso
          Não deixe cair nada no chão. ― Don't let anything fall to the floor.
        3. (poetic) land
          Synonym: terra
          Este é o nosso chão. ― This is our land.
        4. (geography, obsolete) plain
          Synonym: chã
        5. (Brazil, informal) a period of time between the present and a future event
          Synonym: tempo
          Ainda tem um chão até o dia de eu me mudar. ― There is still some time until the day I will move.
        Derived terms
        [edit]
        • rés do chão

        [edit]
        • Chã
        • Chãos
        • Chãs
        Descendants
        [edit]
        • Macanese: cham, (modern spelling) chám

        Etymology 2

        [edit]

          Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese chão (“flat, smooth”), from Latin plānus. Doublet of plano, piano, and lhano

          Adjective

          [edit]

          chão (feminine chã, masculine plural chãos, feminine plural chãs)

          1. (archaic) flat, level, even, smooth
            Synonyms: plano, liso, nivelado
          Derived terms
          [edit]
          • Vila Chã

          • “chão”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

          Noun

          1. (in compounds) frog

          Derived terms
